title: Enthusiastic Firing Training Conducted at CATC–I Camp
content: As part of the Combined Annual Training Camp (CATC–I) being organized by the 23(A) Battalion NCC at St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala , a firing training session was conducted on Wednesday. The training aimed to enhance the cadets’ shooting skills, which are an essential component of military training. The firing practice was closely supervised by Camp Commandant Colonel Gopal Tripathi and Deputy Camp Commandant Lieutenant Colonel N.S. Parmar , who provided valuable guidance and instructions to both the staff and cadets. They emphasized that adherence to safety protocols, discipline, and accuracy in target shooting are vital qualities every cadet must develop. Before the practical session, cadets were given detailed instructions on weapon handling, safety regulations, precautions during firing, aiming techniques, breathing control, and trigger control. Following the briefing, the cadets participated in a structured firing practice session at the firing range, where their skills and performance were assessed. The training was conducted under the supervision of Subedar Major Ranveer Singh, Camp Adjutant Major Y. Anji Reddy, Training JCO Subedar Ravindra Singh, Associate NCC Officer Lieutenant Medikonda Rajesh Babu, BHM P. Ramesh, and Havildar Ramesh . Cadets participated with great enthusiasm and dedication. Officials stated that cadets who demonstrated outstanding performance during the firing practice would be shortlisted to represent the 23rd Andhra Battalion in the Six-District Level Firing Selection Competitions scheduled to be held on June 19 and 21 . The officials further noted that firing training plays a crucial role in developing concentration, self-confidence, discipline, patience, and leadership qualities among cadets. They also informed that, as part of the camp, training programs on drill, map reading, field craft, personality development, and yoga are being conducted alongside other activities.

title: CATC–I NCC Training Camp Inaugurated at St. Ann’s College, Chirala
content: The Combined Annual Training Camp–I (CATC–I), organized under the aegis of the 23 Andhra Pradesh Battalion NCC, was inaugurated with great enthusiasm today at St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala. Addressing the cadets during the opening ceremony, Camp Commandant Colonel Gopal Tripathi emphasized the vital role of NCC in shaping disciplined, patriotic, and responsible young citizens. He stated that NCC training significantly contributes to developing leadership qualities, self-confidence, discipline, and a spirit of service among cadets. He encouraged all participants to make the best use of the training opportunities provided during the camp and strive for excellence. Highlighting the importance of the camp, Colonel Tripathi noted that it serves as a crucial platform for the selection of cadets for the prestigious Thal Sainik Camp (TSC). He described TSC as one of the most esteemed NCC events in the country and urged cadets to actively participate in activities such as drill, map reading, tent pitching, obstacle training, firing, and other competitive events to showcase their abilities. He further advised cadets to approach competitions with true sportsmanship, focusing not merely on winning or losing but on learning, teamwork, mutual cooperation, and discipline. He encouraged every cadet to give their best performance, as outstanding participants would have the opportunity to advance to higher-level selections for the Thal Sainik Camp. He also explained how NCC training helps build leadership skills, confidence, and dedication towards national service. On the occasion, Deputy Camp Commandant Lieutenant Colonel N. S. Parmar briefed the cadets about the camp schedule and training modules. He informed them that the camp would include training sessions on drill, weapon training, map reading, field craft, personality development, leadership, sports, and cultural activities. The inaugural function was attended by Subedar Major Ranveer Singh, Camp Adjutant Major Y. Anji Reddy, Lieutenant Medikonda Rajesh Babu, First Officers P. Suresh Babu and T. Venkateswarlu, Second Officer G. Gopinath, Training JCO Ravindra Singh, and BHM P. Ramesh. A large number of NCC cadets from various educational institutions participated enthusiastically in the opening ceremony, making the event a grand success.

title: 🏆 St. Ann’s Teams Shine at National-Level Volleyball & Kabaddi Championships
content: Students of St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology brought great pride to the institution by securing top positions in national-level sports competitions held at Ongole. The teams emerged as winners at the PACE Festino 2K26 , a National Youth Festival organized by PACE Institute of Technology and Sciences . According to College Secretary Vanama Ramakrishna Rao and Correspondent S. Lakshmana Rao , the achievement reflects the students’ excellence not only in academics but also in sports. Principal Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu stated that the men’s volleyball team competed among 16 teams and clinched victory by defeating the host PACE team in the finals. The winning volleyball team included R. Ramana, G.V.R. Teja Reddy, K. Andrews, G. Michael, K. Dani, K. Sai Kumar, and M. Revanth Venkata Mani Kumar , as informed by Physical Director Annam Srinivasa Rao . Similarly, in the women’s kabaddi category, 15 teams participated, and St. Ann’s team emerged as champions by defeating the PACE team in the finals. The winning team members included V. Manasa, K. Anita, B. Pravallika, B. Shruti Pavani, P. Harini, T. Srividya, D. Ramya, M. Shravani, M. Sonali, G. Sripoojitha, M. Anita, and C. Sanjana . On this occasion, a felicitation ceremony was held in the college premises. Administrative Manager R.V. Ramanamurthy , Director (Accreditations) Dr. C. Subba Rao , Director (Administration) Vanama Dora Naga Sainath , along with department heads, faculty, and students, congratulated both teams for their remarkable achievement. 👉 With consistent excellence in both academics and sports, St. Ann’s College continues to foster all-round development among its students.

title: 📰 Free Study Material Distributed to Polytechnic Entrance Aspirants
content: Free study material was distributed on Friday to students attending the free Polytechnic Entrance coaching at St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology . This was informed by College Secretary Vanama Ramakrishna Rao and Correspondent S. Lakshmana Rao . Principal Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu stated that all students preparing for POLYCET–2026 were provided with complete study material required for their training. He also mentioned that experienced faculty members are offering quality coaching to help students succeed in the entrance examination. Deputy Director of St. Ann’s Polytechnic College, Dr. K. Vijay Bhaskara Reddy , said that along with regular classes, model exams based on the POLYCET–2026 pattern are being conducted daily. He encouraged interested students to join the coaching program. First Year In-charge S. Amaranath Babu informed that free bus facility is being provided for students coming from Chirala, Bapatla, and nearby areas. Students interested in joining this free coaching program can register by contacting 9505518288 or 7207123457 and attend the classes. On this occasion, Dr. C. Subba Rao (Director – Accreditations), Vanama Dora Naga Sainath (Director – Administration), faculty members, and students participated in the program.

title: 📰 Six-Day Workshop on AI & ML using Power BI Concludes at St. Ann’s
content: six-day workshop on “AI & ML using Power BI” was successfully conducted at St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology , as informed by College Secretary Vanama Ramakrishna Rao and Correspondent Srimanthula Lakshmana Rao . Principal Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu stated that the workshop was organized for second-year B.Tech students of the Cyber Security department in collaboration with the Andhra Pradesh State Skill Development Corporation (APSSDC) . Resource person E. Prem Kumar from APSSDC actively participated in the workshop, as mentioned by Head of the Cyber Security Department Dr. S. Indraneel . He further explained that Artificial Intelligence helps in enhancing decision-making abilities and achieving defined goals effectively. The workshop provided practical exposure on how AI and Machine Learning can be integrated with Power BI to improve productivity in various organizations. Students were also given hands-on experience through practical experiments and real-time applications. Speaking at the valedictory session, the Principal emphasized the growing importance of AI & ML in solving real-world problems and improving organizational performance using Power BI. He highlighted that acquiring knowledge in these emerging technologies would help students secure better career opportunities in the near future. On this occasion, Dr. C. Subba Rao (Director – Accreditations), Vanama Dora Naga Sainath (Director – Administration), heads of various departments, faculty members, and students participated in the closing ceremony.

title: 📰 Six-Day Workshop on ServiceNow Tool Successfully Concludes at St. Ann’s, Chirala (2026)
content: A six-day workshop on the ServiceNow Tool was successfully conducted at St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala , as announced jointly by College Secretary Vanama Ramakrishna Rao and Correspondent Srimanthula Lakshmana Rao on Tuesday. Principal Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu stated that the workshop was organized by the Department of Computer Science & Engineering for B.Tech second and third-year students over the past six days. The workshop was conducted under the guidance of the Department of Computer Science & Engineering in association with the Computer Society of India (CSI) and with the support of Next Gen, Secunderabad . It was delivered as a six-day global certification course on the ServiceNow tool under the supervision of J. Vamsi Krishna , as informed by Head of the CSE Department Dr. P. Harini . During the workshop, students were provided with in-depth knowledge of the ServiceNow platform along with practical exposure and hands-on sessions. The program helped students understand real-time applications and usage of the tool in the modern IT industry. Addressing the students at the valedictory session, the Principal emphasized the growing importance of the ServiceNow tool in today’s advanced computing world. He encouraged students to focus on such emerging technologies to secure better career opportunities. T. Shesha Sai served as the workshop coordinator. On this occasion, Dr. C. Subba Rao (Director – Accreditations), Vanama Dora Naga Sainath (Director – Administration), faculty members of the CSE department, and students participated in the closing ceremony.

title: Blood Donation Camp Organized by NSS at St. Ann’s College
content: A blood donation camp was successfully organized on Wednesday at St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology under the auspices of the National Service Scheme (NSS) unit. This was jointly announced by the College Secretary, Vanama Ramakrishna Rao, and Correspondent, Srimanthula Lakshmana Rao. The camp was inaugurated by the Principal, Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu. Speaking on the occasion, he emphasized that blood donation is the greatest of all donations and is equal to saving a life. He appreciated the students for voluntarily coming forward to donate blood and highlighted that such noble acts help save lives during emergencies. On this occasion, B. Mahesh Babu, a final-year B.Tech student from the Civil Engineering department, was honored for donating blood voluntarily 10 times. More than 100 students participated enthusiastically and donated blood in the camp. Doctors and staff from the Government Area Hospital, Chirala, including Dr. Raja Selvan and Blood Bank In-charge U. Tirumala Rao, took part in the camp. The camp was organized under the guidance of NSS Program Officer Dr. D. Jyothi Swaroop along with NSS coordinators. The event was attended by Dr. C. Subba Rao (Director – Accreditations), Vanama Dora Naga Sainath (Director – Administration), heads of departments, faculty members, and students.

title: MoU Signed Between St. Ann’s College and Ramsur Agri LLP
content: St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, Chirala, has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Ramsur Agri LLP. This was jointly announced by the College Secretary, Vanama Ramakrishna Rao, and Correspondent, Srimanthula Lakshmana Rao. According to the College Principal, Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu, the MoU has been signed between the Mechanical Engineering Department of St. Ann’s College and Ramsur Agri LLP. He stated that this collaboration aims to enhance students’ exposure to emerging technologies. Head of the Mechanical Engineering Department, Dr. Lakshmi Tulasi Chavali, explained that this agreement will provide students with opportunities in drone technologies and other emerging fields , along with internships, training programs, and project development support. She also mentioned that the MoU will remain in effect for a period of three years . On this occasion, heads of various departments, faculty members, and students expressed their happiness and appreciation for this collaboration, which is expected to benefit students with practical knowledge and industry exposure.

title: Week-Long Workshop on “Application of Advanced Tools in Land Survey” Begins at St. Ann’s College
content: A week-long workshop on “Application of Advanced Tools in Land Survey” has commenced at St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, Chirala. This was jointly announced by the College Secretary, Vanama Ramakrishna Rao, and Correspondent, Srimanthula Lakshmana Rao. The workshop is being organized by the Civil Engineering Department from March 16, 2026 , for B.Tech students, as informed by the Principal, Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu. The program is being conducted in collaboration with Unique Survey Solutions, Vijayawada , under the guidance of T. Prem Babu, said Head of the Civil Engineering Department, Dr. T. Kiran Kumar. During the workshop, students will gain hands-on training and awareness on advanced land surveying tools such as Total Station, Trimble, GeoMax, and DGPS equipment . Addressing the gathering, the Principal emphasized the importance of land surveying in the field of civil engineering and encouraged students to develop expertise in modern survey tools to enhance their career opportunities. At the inaugural session, Director (Accreditations) Dr. C. Subba Rao, Director (Administration) Vanama Dora Naga Sainath, along with faculty members of the Civil Engineering Department and students, participated in the program.

title: 3-Day Workshop on Drone Technology Begins at St. Ann’s College
content: A three-day workshop on Drone Technology has been inaugurated at St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, Chirala. This was jointly announced by the College Secretary, Vanama Ramakrishna Rao, and Correspondent, Srimanthula Lakshmana Rao. The workshop is being organized by the Mechanical Engineering Department from March 16, 2026 , for B.Tech second and third-year students, as informed by the Principal, Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu. The program is being conducted in collaboration with Ramsur Agri LLP , under the guidance of K. Manoj Kumar, said Head of the Mechanical Engineering Department, Dr. Lakshmi Tulasi Chavali. During the workshop, students will gain awareness and practical exposure to drone technology , including hands-on experiments and applications. Addressing the gathering, the Principal highlighted the growing importance of drone technology in the modern technological world and encouraged students to focus on this field to secure better career opportunities. The workshop is coordinated by P. Harish and B. Ravi Kumar. At the inaugural session, Director (Accreditations) Dr. C. Subba Rao, Director (Administration) Vanama Dora Naga Sainath, faculty members of the Mechanical Engineering Department, and students participated in the program.

title: Parent–Teacher Meeting Conducted by Mechanical Engineering Department at St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology
content: The Department of Mechanical Engineering, St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala , organized a Parent–Teacher Meeting on January 27, 2026 , with the objective of strengthening coordination between parents and faculty members and reviewing students’ academic progress. The programme was conducted under the guidance of the college management. Parents were warmly welcomed and briefed about the academic performance, attendance, discipline, and overall development of their wards. Faculty members interacted directly with parents and discussed students’ strengths, areas of improvement, and future academic goals. During the meeting, emphasis was laid on the importance of parental involvement in students’ education and on fostering a supportive environment for academic excellence and personal growth. The event witnessed active participation from parents, faculty members, and students of the Mechanical Engineering Department , making the programme informative and productive.

title: St. Ann’s Management with Winners of VTM-3 Cricket Tournament
content: The JNTU-K Kakinada Central Zone Men’s Cricket Tournament is being conducted at St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology , according to a statement issued by College Secretary Mr. Vanama Ramakrishna Rao and College Correspondent Mr. Srimanthula Lakshmana Rao . The Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Kakinada Central Zone Men’s Cricket Tournament, which also serves as an Inter-College Tournament and University Team Selections , commenced at the college on Monday, said College Principal Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu . He informed that the tournament is being conducted over a period of three days . On the third day of the tournament , Dr. Tulasi Ram from Tulasi Hospital, Chirala , and Dr. Srikanth from Poorvi Scanning Centre attended as Chief Guests and formally inaugurated the matches. In the matches held on the third day, the first match was played between St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology and VSM Engineering College, Ramachandrapuram . In this match, St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology emerged victorious . VSM Engineering College, after opting to bat first, scored 68 runs , while St. Ann’s College successfully chased the target by scoring 69 runs , winning the match by eight wickets , informed Physical Education Lecturer Mr. Annam Srinivasa Rao . He further stated that the second match of the day was being played between GIET Engineering College and Loyola Engineering College . On this occasion, the management of St. Ann’s College congratulated the winning team , appreciating their performance and sportsmanship.

title: 77th Republic Day Celebrated with Grandeur at St. Ann’s Group of Colleges, Chirala
content: The 77th Republic Day celebrations were conducted with great enthusiasm at St. Ann’s Group of Colleges, Chirala , according to a joint statement issued by College Secretary Mr. Vanama Ramakrishna Rao and College Correspondent Mr. Srimanthula Lakshmana Rao . On this occasion, College Principal Dr. K. Jagadeesh Babu hoisted the National Flag and addressed the gathering, highlighting the significance of the Indian Republic and the values enshrined in the Constitution of India . He urged the youth to understand the rights granted by the Constitution and to shoulder their responsibilities with commitment in order to play a crucial role in the nation’s development . Addressing the gathering, Principal of the College of Pharmacy, Dr. V. V. Nageswara Rao , emphasized that the youth have a vital role in shaping the future and development of the country. On the occasion of Republic Day, prizes were distributed to students who emerged victorious in various competitions conducted as part of the celebrations. The flag hoisting and ceremonial proceedings were conducted under the supervision of Physical Education Lecturer Mr. Annam Srinivasa Rao . The programme was attended by Dr. C. Subba Rao (Director – Accreditations) , Mr. V. Dora Naga Sainadh (Director – Administration) , heads of various departments, faculty members, and students.
